other_failure_modes.name: pandas_index_alignment_bug
other_failure_modes.description: During target encoding, a pandas Series created from a numpy target array (which defaults to a 0-indexed range) is grouped by a feature Series that retains the original dataframe indices. Pandas aligns these by index, causing severe target-to-feature misalignment and resulting in mostly NaN or garbage encodings.

other_failure_modes.name: knn_feature_distribution_shift
other_failure_modes.description: When computing KNN distance features, the model queries the training set for nearest neighbors of both train and test samples, then slices off the first neighbor. This correctly removes the self-neighbor for train samples, but incorrectly discards the actual nearest training sample for test samples, causing a fundamental feature distribution shift between train and test.

other_failure_modes.name: categorical_features_treated_as_continuous
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical columns are integer-encoded (Label Encoding) and horizontally stacked into a numpy array before being passed to LightGBM and CatBoost. Because the categorical feature indices are not specified to the model APIs, the algorithms treat these nominal integers as continuous numerical features.

summary: The agent implements a highly advanced pipeline featuring custom spatial engineering, a PyTorch ResNet, and an optimized ensemble, successfully avoiding all standard predefined failure modes. However, the solution is severely compromised by a pandas index alignment bug during in-fold target encoding, which misaligns targets with features. Additionally, there is a subtle train-test distribution shift introduced by incorrectly slicing KNN distances for test samples.
